subtopics.title: Labelling Triangles and the Area Rule

questions.question: In the standard labelling of triangle ABC, small letter a names:
options: The side between A and B

questions.question: In Area = ½ab·sin C, the angle C must be:
options: The largest angle of the triangle
The included angle — wedged between sides a and b

questions.question: The area rule is derived by:
options: Doubling the triangle into a rectangle
Applying Pythagoras to the longest side
Dropping a perpendicular so the height becomes a·sin C inside ½ × base × height

subtopics.title: Proving and Using the Sine Rule

questions.question: The sine rule is proved by:
options: Setting the three versions of the area rule equal and dividing by ½abc
Applying the cosine rule three times

questions.question: The sine rule needs, at minimum:
options: One complete opposite pair — a side with its facing angle — plus one more piece
Two sides and the included angle

questions.question: With A = 35°, B = 70° and b = 14 cm, side a equals:
The 'unknown on top' habit means:
options: Always writing the largest side first
Putting the answer in the numerator of the final fraction is wrong
Writing angles above sides in every fraction
Choosing the version of the rule that seats the unknown in the numerator, so the last line is a multiplication

subtopics.title: Finding Angles with the Sine Rule

questions.question: With a = 12, b = 8 and A = 48°, sin B equals:
The calculator's inverse sine only ever returns:
options: An acute angle — even though a second-quadrant angle shares the same sine

questions.question: The second candidate for angle B, at 180° − 29,70° = 150,30°, is rejected because:
options: It is not a whole number
150,30° + 48° already exceeds 180°, so no triangle can hold it
Obtuse angles never occur in triangles

questions.question: The habit demanded after every inverse-sine result is:
options: Rounding it to the nearest degree
Taking its cosine as a cross-check
Computing 180° minus the angle, testing it against the angle sum, and recording the verdict

subtopics.title: Multi-Step Problems — Chaining the Two Rules

questions.question: Given A = 44°, B = 58° and c = 20 cm, the area rule cannot fire immediately because:
options: Only one side is known — the rule's price is two sides plus the included angle
The sine rule must always run twice first

questions.question: The first step of the chain, angle C, comes free from:
options: 180° − 44° − 58° = 78° — the angle sum of a triangle

questions.question: Side a is then built as:
The final area line uses angle B = 58° because:
options: B was given first in the question
58° has the largest sine of the three angles
Sides a and c meet at vertex B — read off the sketch, so B is the included angle

questions.question: In the gate picture, sine of the included angle plays the role of:
options: The squash factor — 1 at 90°, shrinking towards 0 as the gate folds flat
The length of the longer arm
The number of cells in the gate

questions.question: At exactly 90°, the area rule gives:
options: The maximum area, since sin 90° = 1 — and the formula reduces to ½ × base × height

questions.question: At 0° or 180°, the triangle's area is:
options: Half the product of the arms
Zero — the arms lie flat and sine reads 0

questions.question: The one fatal error with the area rule is:
options: Grabbing an angle that is not wedged between the two given sides

subtopics.title: Fair Trade at the Triangle Market

questions.question: The trade agreement every triangle honours is:
options: The bigger the angle, the longer the side facing it
All sides trade at different rates
The shortest side faces the largest angle

questions.question: The market's fixed exchange rate is set by:
options: One complete pair — a known side over the sine of its facing angle, here 14 over sin 70°
The average of all three sides

questions.question: Once the rate is fixed, side a is bought as:
options: sin 35° — its own facing angle — times the rate, giving 8,55

questions.question: The 'second suspect' hiding behind every inverse sine is:
options: The angle's complement at 90° minus the answer
The angle at 180° minus the answer, wearing the same sine

subtopics.title: Planning the Route Before You Drive

questions.question: Multi-step planning starts by:
options: Taking stock — known sides, known angles, complete pairs, and what the destination formula needs
Choosing the rule with the shortest name

questions.question: The area rule's fixed fare is:
options: Two sides plus the angle wedged between them

questions.question: The route in the worked example ran:
options: Area rule first, then two sine rules
Free third angle (78°), sine rule for the second side (14,20), area rule to finish (120,45 cm²)
Three applications of the sine rule

questions.question: Stating which rule is used and why, at every step, matters because:
options: It lengthens the answer to look thorough
It is required only for the cosine rule
It replaces the need for a sketch
The written reason earns its own credit and forces the entitlement check
